basic_identification.full_title: Stainless Steel Sliding Door Bolts ( Aldrops ) for Use with Padlocks — Specification (First Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Civil Engineering / Builder's Hardware (approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Builder's Hardware Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies the material, mechanical, manufacturing, dimensional, and finish requirements for clip-type stainless steel sliding door bolts (commonly known as aldrops) used in general building construction for locking doors, gates, and similar assemblies with padlocks.

revision_history.edition: First Revision (reorganized to incorporate modifications based on industry experience, updating testing parameters and expanding material grade allowances)

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Bolts, Nuts and Fasteners (Quality Control) Order' (including subsequent QCO updates) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all Stainless Steel Sliding Door Bolts (Aldrops) for Use with Padlocks must conform to IS 15834 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or selling uncertified door aldrops is a statutory offense. Micro and small scale units are granted specific delayed implementation schedules, and export shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial alloy door fixtures.

requirements.detail: Every sliding door bolt conforming to this standard must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) under a valid licence issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards, along with the registered licence number (CM/L).
As illustrated in Fig. 1, the sliding door aldrop assembly comprises: a sliding bolt, hasp (with slot), clip, and staple, constructed dynamically to allow secure padlock locking.

requirements.requirement_type: Permitted Materials and Stainless Steel Grades
requirements.detail: In the First Revision (2020), raw material specifications have been modified, permitting the use of any standard stainless steel grade of suitable quality (e.g., standard Grades X07Cr18Ni9 sheet or X04Cr13 wire rods) provided the finished aldrop complies with all physical, mechanical, and corrosion resistance requirements.
The nominal diameter of the sliding bolt ($D$) must be 12 mm, 14 mm, 16 mm, or 19 mm as specified by the purchaser.

The thickness of the constituent steel sheets ($t$) must be: a) minimum 2.20 mm for 12 mm and 14 mm diameter bolts; b) minimum 2.50 mm for 16 mm and 19 mm diameter bolts to prevent mechanical deformation under load.
The hasp must have a width of $40 \pm 1$ mm, length of $110 \pm 2$ mm, and a slot width of minimum 6 mm. The hasp tab length below the bolt center must be at least 65 mm.

The clip must have a width of $20 \pm 1$ mm and height of $60 \pm 2$ mm with a 7 mm square hole for a carriage bolt. The staple must have a width of $35 \pm 0.5$ mm, height of $45 \pm 1$ mm, projection of $30 \pm 2$ mm, and a hole diameter of $13 \pm 0.5$ mm.
Each aldrop must be clearly and legibly marked with the manufacturer's name/trade-mark and the words 'Stainless Steel' permanently imprinted.
The products must be packed in cartons. Each carton must bear a secure label displaying: manufacturer's name, size, grade of materials used, quantity, batch number, and date of manufacture.
All sliding door bolts of the identical type, material, and size manufactured in a single day constitute a lot. Random samples must be selected as per Table 1 for physical-mechanical auditing.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 15834 : 2020 is the strict national Indian Standard safety specification regulating stainless steel sliding door bolts (aldrops) designed for use with padlocks in general building construction. Under India's mandatory national Bolts, Nuts and Fasteners Quality Control Order (QCO), all such stainless steel aldrops manufactured, imported, or sold in India must carry the Bureau of Indian Standards Standard Mark (ISI Mark). It outlines exact dimensional and thickness boundaries—including sliding bolt diameters (12 to 19 mm) and hasp/clip clearances—and specifies standard mechanical and testing protocols (tensile strength, dimensional accuracy, and corrosion resistance). The standard ensures that the hardware remains rust-proof, durable, and structurally reliable in high-humidity or coastal environments.
